title: Judge Orders Bench Warrant for Michael Dean Davis Jr. in 2024 Child-Endangerment Case
excerpt: A Webb County district judge has reactivated the child-endangerment case against Michael Dean Davis Jr., who is jailed in Leon County on a murder charge, and issued a bench warrant to bring him to court in Laredo for a status hearing Dec. 2.
content:
A Webb County district judge has reactivated the child-endangerment case against Michael Dean Davis Jr., a man jailed in Leon County on a murder charge, and issued a bench warrant to bring him to court in Laredo, according to court records.

Judge Jose A. Lopez of the 49th District Court ordered the warrant and set a status hearing for Dec. 2. As of Oct. 9, the state had confirmed the victim still wished to move forward with the case.

Davis is charged with abandoning or endangering a child, a state jail felony that carries 180 days to two years in a state jail and a fine of up to $10,000. He has not been convicted of the charge, and the presumption of innocence applies.

The charge stems from his arrest in Laredo in November 2024. On Nov. 12, 2024, the Laredo Police Department joined the U.S. Marshals Service and the Leon County Sheriff’s Office in following a tip that Davis and his 8-year-old son were living in the 3200 block of Simmental Drive, near Cuatro Vientos. Officers served a search warrant at the home that evening and arrested Davis on the murder warrant without incident. Authorities said he had lived in Laredo for about two years.

The boy was not hurt, but the arrest affidavit describes trash and food wrappers throughout the home, mold in the kitchen sink, feces in a bathroom and toilet, marijuana on a table, and loaded rifles and magazines within the child’s reach. Lab work at Laredo Medical Center later showed the child tested positive for marijuana, court documents state.

In Leon County, Davis faces charges of murder and aggravated kidnapping. That case began in June 2024 with a report of a woman and child whom relatives had not heard from since July 2022. On Oct. 22, 2024, Leon County investigators searched a property in Buffalo, Texas, and recovered human remains later identified as Mahogany Washington, 27, the mother of Davis’ son. Davis was named a suspect and remains in the Leon County Jail awaiting trial, custody records show.

The Dec. 2 status hearing is the next step in the Webb County case. Webb Watch 956 will follow what happens there.

Sources: 49th District Court, Webb County — bench warrant and case records; Leon County Sheriff’s Office custody records; Laredo Police Department arrest records, Nov. 12, 2024
